chapter: Learning piano, dancing and Alphonso Trent
title: Okmulgee: Oscar Pettiford's family band, Walter Page and the Blue Devils
summary: In Okmulgee he first sees Oscar Pettiford and meets Walter Page and Hot Lips Page; he plays and gambles around local bands and names Texas local lights.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: They had a family band, yeah. A family band in Okmulgee, Oklahoma. And that's when I first saw him. And then I met Walter Page. Walter Page and Willie Lewis had the Blue Devils and they had a good band. Hot Lips Page later joined them in Tulsa. And then I just became ......., but I was playing more and more... not for money. I used to just play and give the money to the other person. If they would say, 'it's bad and we want you to play tonight, will you help us out?' 'Yeah.' They'd have seven, eight musicians...didn't get much money anyway. And I could gamble--you know what I mean--I knew all those things, you know, how to gamble...and I could go some place and dance and get extra money. So I would go and play with the

band. And you know, Budd Johnson and Buster Smith, Dad Minor—I don't know if you know who Dad Minor is, he's a trombone player ...Dan Minor and John R. Davis and Willie Owens...these were all local lights, but they were well known. Like you had another segment in Dallas, like Troy Floyd and Benny Long and people like that who went with Trent, and Benno Kennedy and these musicians...
